messages:
alex.sre: Heads-up — scheduling a targeted maintenance to apply a small kernel/CUDA micropatch on GPU serving nodes. Window: 2026-04-02 02:00-03:00 UTC (canary then stagger). Scope: start canary in us-west1 GPU pool, then roll per-region. Expected impact: brief p99 spikes (~+200–400ms) for short windows during pod restarts (typical 3–7m per node). We'll route heavy-tail traffic to CPU/model-variant fallbacks during canary. Updating SLO tolerance for the window. See runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/gpu-kernel-maint-2026. Oncall please ack.

priya-ops: Ack. I'll run prechecks, drain the canary node, and execute warmup. Posting pre-check checklist in 15m.

dave-sre: Copy. Rollback criteria I'm using: p99 > 600ms sustained > 3m OR error rate increase > 0.5% absolute. Monitoring targets: grafana panel linked in runbook. Smoke test and commands below.

dave-sre: ```
# cordon and drain a single GPU node (canary)
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 -n inference
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
# restart daemonset to pick up kernel image
kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/gpu-serving-pool
# smoke test (local)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"input":"smoke"}' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate | jq .
```

rita-platform: I'll set FF_CLUSTER_AUTOROLL=false and pause cluster auto-rollouts for the maintenance window. Also enabling model-fallback routing tag for canary traffic (tag: maintenance-fallback).

sam-eng: Noting product owners — recommend enabling tiny-model fallback for long-running sessions during the window. I'll publish a short status page update and ping Sales for any Dedicated customers who need pre-notice.

mktg: Drafting the external status blurb now. Send any customer impact bullets and estimated duration (we have 1h window; impact is brief per-node restarts).

productops: Quick Q — Do we exempt Dedicated reserved pools from this by default? Some customers have strict SLA language.

alex.sre: We will NOT include Dedicated pools with SLA=true in the automated drain by default. To include them you must add the pool to allowed-drain in the runbook and get sign-off from Customer Success. Default behavior: exempt.

oncall-bot: oncall: dave-sre assigned for 02:00-03:30 UTC. Reminder: use runbook gpu-kernel-maint-2026 and escalation path.

priya-ops: I'll also post a 1h reminder to #customer-success and #support. Will add the rollback checklist to the runbook now.

dave-sre: PromQL snippets I'll be watching:

```
# token gen p99 for inference route
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[5m])) by (le))

# error rate
sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference",code!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference"}[5m]))
```

dave-sre: If p99 > 600ms for 03:00 consecutive minutes OR error rate > 0.005 then immediate rollback and failover to warm pool.

alex.sre: TL;DR: maintenance 2026-04-02 02:00-03:00 UTC, canary us-west1 then stagger, expected short p99 spikes during pod restarts; rollback criteria p99 >600ms >3m or error rate >0.5%. Acks from: @dave-sre @priya-ops @rita-platform @sam-eng. Please react with :white_check_mark: when you have tasks covered.
thread_text: GPU kernel/CUDA micropatch maintenance + SLO tolerance update
